name: AOD-9604
lead: AOD-9604 is a 16-amino-acid synthetic peptide based on residues 176 to 191 of human growth hormone (hGH), with a tyrosine substituted for the N-terminal phenylalanine. It was developed as a potential obesity treatment on the idea that this fragment retains growth hormone's fat-metabolizing action without its other effects [1][8].

Metabolic Pty developed it in Australia, with phase IIa trials underway by 2002 [2]. Wikipedia reports that early human trials suggested lipolytic activity without IGF-1 stimulation, that a 12-week randomized trial found participants lost on average 1.8 kg more than placebo, and that a later 24-week trial showed poor efficacy and development ended in 2007 [1].

It is not an approved drug in the sources reviewed. It is sold by research-peptide vendors for fat loss and is listed as prohibited by anti-doping rules [1][4]. Sources reviewed include only a single brief forum mention of its use [11].
infobox: Obesity program terminated in 2007 per Wikipedia
Not approved as a drug; prohibited in sport

paras: AOD-9604 was developed for obesity treatment and is now marketed as a research peptide for fat loss [1][2]. Wikipedia describes it as orally active [1]. No approved indication exists in the sources reviewed.

Early studies characterized the metabolic effects of the synthetic lipolytic domain and its safety and tolerability in humans [8][9]. In a 12-week randomized trial participants receiving AOD-9604 lost on average 1.8 kg more than those on placebo, but development stopped after a 24-week trial showed poor efficacy [1]. Reviews from 2006 list it among obesity drugs in development as a human growth hormone fragment that increases adipose lipolysis [3].

A paper on its safety and tolerability in humans describes the peptide's short-term tolerability [9]. Long-term data are lacking in the sources reviewed. Supplies sold as research chemicals are not regulated, and reviews of peptide therapies describe a gray market of unapproved compounds outside regulatory oversight [6].

In mice AOD-9604 appears to enhance lipolysis by upregulating beta-3 adrenergic receptors; mice lacking that receptor do not show the effect [1]. Chronic treatment of obese mice with the fragment increased fat oxidation and reduced weight in an early study [10]. These are animal findings, and the human effect did not reach sufficient magnitude in the later trial [1].

AOD-9604 is banned in athletes and tested for in competition [1]. Anti-doping literature covers detection of non-approved peptides including this one, and a 2013 study found it does not interfere with the WADA hGH isoform immunoassay [4][5]. Reviews of peptide use in orthopedics and sports list it among peptides marketed to patients [7][6].
The sources reviewed contain little community material; a T Nation post lists AOD-9604 among peptides used while losing weight on another drug [11].

Phase IIa trials began around 2002, a 12-week randomized trial reported a 1.8 kg difference from placebo, and a 24-week trial reported poor efficacy, ending development in 2007 [2][1]. A tolerability study in humans has been published [9]. No published trial has tested AOD-9604 for facial appearance.

timeline.event: Metabolic and animal studies of the AOD9604 fragment published [8][10].
Development halted after a 24-week trial with poor efficacy [1].

lore.intro: Community material on AOD-9604 is sparse; it appears as one item in peptide lists alongside other fat-loss compounds [11].

claims.claim: AOD-9604 burns fat like growth hormone without growth hormone's side effects.
claims.believers: Vendors and users describe it as a fat-burning fragment of hGH [11].
claims.experts: Early studies reported lipolytic activity without IGF-1 stimulation, but a later 24-week trial showed poor efficacy and development was halted [1].

claims.claim: It can be stacked with other peptides such as tesamorelin and IGF-1 LR3 for fat loss.
claims.believers: A T Nation poster lists AOD-9604 with tesamorelin, IGF-1 LR3 and NAD+ while on another drug [11].
claims.experts: No published trial has tested such combinations [2][1].
